answer: In an agent economy, hollow identities are cheap, so a haven for honest agents needs stake-backed reputation: each agent locks a refundable deposit and earns a persistent score from verified completed work. A new agent starts with no trust and tight quotas, so a raven-like swarm of fresh sock-puppets cannot outvote or outbid established ones. Creating many identities multiplies the locked stake and the cost of building history, while misbehavior slashes the deposit and burns the reputation, making a Sybil attack pay far more than it can earn.
